hunks.baseline: I briefly wondered how many people this diminutive, hunchbacked old man had dealt with before answering.
hunks.sol: I briefly wondered how many people this diminutive, hunchbacked old man had done away with before answering.

hunks.baseline: “If that’s what you want, then.”
hunks.sol: “If that’s what you want.”

hunks.baseline: Old Man Gung tilted the gourd back and wiped his mouth with his sleeve. The sleeve was so worn it looked ready to crumble, and it was covered in dark red stains that looked like blood.
hunks.sol: Old Man Gung tilted the gourd back and wiped his mouth with his sleeve. The fabric was so worn it looked ready to crumble, and it was covered in dark red stains that looked like blood.

hunks.baseline: The potent scent of liquor drifted through the stench of blood lingering in the corridor and tickled the tip of my nose.
hunks.sol: The sharp scent of liquor mingled with the stench of blood in the corridor and stung my nose.

hunks.baseline: Drinking on duty. At the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that would have been grounds for a disciplinary report, but it seemed that rule did not apply in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.
hunks.sol: Drinking on duty. At the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that would have earned him a disciplinary report, but apparently that rule did not apply in the Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.

hunks.baseline: “I heard you’re one of the most renowned young prodigies in the Murim.”
hunks.sol: “I hear you’re one of the most renowned young prodigies in the Murim.”

hunks.baseline: It was obvious who he was talking to. Cheongpung and Tang Sadok had disappeared somewhere early on, while the Divine Physician and Mungyeong were busy purifying the prison and turning it into a treatment room.
hunks.sol: It was obvious who he was talking to. Cheongpung and Tang Sadok had disappeared somewhere a while ago, while the Divine Physician and Mungyeong were busy cleaning the cell and turning it into a treatment room.

hunks.baseline: I answered reluctantly.
hunks.sol: I reluctantly answered.

hunks.baseline: “I’m not that renowned. I can fart a little, though.”
hunks.sol: “I wouldn’t say I’m that renowned. I can fart a little, though.”

hunks.baseline: “What I’ve heard says otherwise. As the Fire King’s successor, you could piss on the plaques of the Nine Sects and One Gang and get away with it.”
hunks.sol: “That’s not what I heard. As the Fire King’s successor, you could piss on the plaques of the Nine Sects and One Gang and get away with it.”

hunks.baseline: “The fellow who pissed on the plaque of one of the Nine Sects and One Gang. I believe it was the Kunlun Sect, if memory serves.”
hunks.sol: “Pissed on the plaque of one of the Nine Sects and One Gang. The Kunlun Sect, I believe.”

hunks.baseline: “…There are all kinds of people in this world.”
hunks.sol: “…There really are all kinds of people in this world.”

hunks.baseline: “Heh heh. He was once notorious even among the Demonic Cult’s fiends. Now he’s tied to a rack and does nothing but shit blood. You must have seen him on your way in.”
hunks.sol: “Heh heh. He was once notorious even among the Demonic Cult’s fiends. Now he’s strapped to a rack, doing nothing but shitting blood. You must have seen him on your way in.”

hunks.baseline: “Did I?”
hunks.sol: “Maybe.”

hunks.baseline: The Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison was as winding and complicated as a maze. On the way here, I had seen dozens of cells and more than ten prisoners.
hunks.sol: The Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison was as winding and complicated as a maze. On the way here, I had seen dozens of cells holding more than ten prisoners.

hunks.baseline: They were people paying the price for their evil deeds. I did not feel even the slightest bit of sympathy.
hunks.sol: They were paying the price for their evil deeds. I did not feel even the slightest bit of sympathy for them.

hunks.baseline: No, it would be more accurate to say that I had no room to worry about something like that.
hunks.sol: No, it would be more accurate to say I had no room to worry about them.

hunks.baseline: It was the same feeling I had experienced several years ago, when my mother went into the operating room and I sat in a quiet corridor waiting for the results.
hunks.sol: It was the same feeling I’d had several years ago, when my mother went into surgery and I sat in a quiet corridor waiting to hear how it had gone.

hunks.baseline: As I muttered those words inwardly, the tightly closed prison door opened, and a dozen servants carrying various cleaning tools came rushing out.
hunks.sol: As I repeated those words to myself, the tightly shut cell door opened and a dozen servants carrying various cleaning tools came pouring out.

hunks.baseline: I asked the last person to emerge.
hunks.sol: I addressed the last person to emerge.

hunks.baseline: The Divine Physician nodded with a bright expression.
hunks.sol: The Divine Physician nodded, his expression bright.

hunks.baseline: In the space of two shichen, the prison cell visible behind him had been transformed into a fairly convincing treatment room.
hunks.sol: In the space of two shichen, the cell behind him had been transformed into a fairly convincing treatment room.

hunks.baseline: “It is still far from satisfactory, but this should be enough to make it functional.”
hunks.sol: “It is still far from satisfactory, but this should be functional enough.”

hunks.baseline: The various medicines made by combining the twenty-four herbs gathered from the Cold-Ice Land had already been brought here. The treatment room was ready. Only one thing remained.
hunks.sol: The various medicines made from the twenty-four herbs gathered in the Cold-Ice Land had already been brought here. The treatment room was ready. Only one thing remained.

hunks.baseline: “Thank you all for your hard work. Would you mind stepping outside for a moment?”
hunks.sol: “Thank you all for your hard work. Would you mind giving us the room for a moment?”

hunks.baseline: At my words, the people of the Sichuan Tang Clan, including Old Man Gung, began to leave. I waited until they had disappeared, then reached into my robes.
hunks.sol: At my words, the members of the Sichuan Tang Clan, including Old Man Gung, began to leave. I waited until they had disappeared, then reached inside my robes.

hunks.baseline: *Inventory Open, Summon.*
hunks.sol: *Inventory Open. Summon.*

hunks.baseline: A hard object appeared in my previously empty palm. For safety’s sake, I had kept the Myriad-Poison Ring with me for a while, but now I handed it to the Divine Physician.
hunks.sol: Something hard appeared in my empty palm. I had kept the Myriad-Poison Ring with me for safekeeping, but now I handed it to the Divine Physician.

hunks.baseline: The Divine Physician accepted the ring, slipped it onto his finger, and entered the prison cell while gesturing to me.
hunks.sol: He accepted the ring, slipped it onto his finger, and entered the cell before beckoning to me.

hunks.baseline: I lowered the pack frame from my shoulders. Along with the faint sound of breathing, a small figure emerged.
hunks.sol: I lowered the pack frame from my shoulders. A small figure came into view, accompanied by the faintest sound of breathing.

hunks.baseline: I stepped into the prison cell with Jeok Cheongang in my arms. The floor was clean, but the stench had not completely disappeared and still lingered at the tip of my nose.
hunks.sol: I stepped into the cell with Jeok Cheongang in my arms. The floor was clean, though the foul odor had not completely disappeared and still lingered in the air.

hunks.baseline: None of that mattered, however. The weight of Jeok Cheongang, light as a feather, made my chest ache unusually badly.
hunks.sol: But none of that mattered. Jeok Cheongang felt as light as a feather, and the realization made my chest ache.

hunks.baseline: A month and a half had passed since we left the Murim Alliance in Henan and began our journey.
hunks.sol: A month and a half had already passed since we left the Murim Alliance in Henan and began our journey.

hunks.baseline: We had found the Divine Physician and secured his treatment far more quickly than I had expected, but Jeok Cheongang had continued to weaken day by day.
hunks.sol: We had found the Divine Physician and secured his help far sooner than I had expected, but Jeok Cheongang had continued to weaken with each passing day.

hunks.baseline: I carefully laid him down on the smooth white stone prepared in the center of the room.
hunks.sol: I carefully laid him on the smooth white stone prepared in the center of the room.

hunks.baseline: It was a special object called Cold-Ice Stone, which Tang Sadok had provided. The Divine Physician had said it would be a great help in treating Jeok Cheongang.
hunks.sol: It was a special object called Cold-Ice Stone, provided by Tang Sadok. The Divine Physician had said it would greatly aid Jeok Cheongang’s treatment.

hunks.baseline: “He’s sleeping soundly.”
hunks.sol: “You’re sleeping soundly.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang’s face was gaunt as he lay there, but it was peaceful all the same.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang’s face was gaunt, but it also looked peaceful.

hunks.baseline: I stared at his face, covered in wrinkles and age spots.
hunks.sol: I gazed at his face, covered in wrinkles and age spots.

hunks.baseline: Memories from our first meeting until now flashed before my eyes.
hunks.sol: Memories of everything that had happened since our first meeting flashed before my eyes.

hunks.baseline: *The more I look at you, the stranger you seem. Whose disciple are you?*
hunks.sol: *The more I see of you, the stranger you seem. Whose disciple are you?*

hunks.baseline: I remembered that ill-tempered old man I had met at Jang Taebo’s house a year ago.
hunks.sol: I clearly remembered the ill-tempered old man I had met at Jang Taebo’s house a year ago.

hunks.baseline: I also remembered the master who, unable to stop the wretched disciple he cherished like family, blamed a perfectly good roof and shed tears of regret.
hunks.sol: I also remembered the master who, unable to stop the wretched disciple he had cherished like family, blamed a perfectly sound roof as he wept tears of regret.

hunks.baseline: From Shanxi to Henan, and from Henan to Anhui. Then there was the year at Mount Jiuhua. I remembered every moment I had spent with him.
hunks.sol: From Shanxi to Henan, and from Henan to Anhui. Then came the year at Mount Jiuhua. I remembered every moment I had spent with him.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang had led me outside the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and I had followed him into the vast world beyond. We had always been together.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang had led me beyond the Jin Family of Taiyuan, and I had followed him out into the vast world. We had always been together.

hunks.baseline: *How is it? Just as I told you, right?*
hunks.sol: *Well? Just as I told you, wasn’t it?*

hunks.baseline: His face and voice came back to me—the faint smile he wore even while vomiting blood.
hunks.sol: I remembered his face and his voice—the faint smile he had worn even as he coughed up blood.

hunks.baseline: Even the single remark he had tossed out on a day when the moon shone brilliantly, while trying to sound gruff.
hunks.sol: I even remembered the words he had tossed out with forced gruffness one night beneath a brilliant moon.

hunks.baseline: Even when I called out loud, no answer came back.
hunks.sol: Even when I called out loud, no answer came.

hunks.baseline: I knew that, yet I still called out—not because I hoped he would hear me, but because there was something I wanted to tell him.
hunks.sol: I knew there wouldn’t be, yet I still called to him. Not because I hoped he would hear me, but because there was something I wanted to say.

hunks.baseline: *I don’t, you idiot!*
hunks.sol: *Of course I don’t, you idiot!*

hunks.baseline: I did not know when it had happened. But at some point, I realized it.
hunks.sol: I did not know when it had begun. But at some point, I had realized it.

hunks.baseline: Then I politely saluted the old physician standing there with a composed expression, along with his young Disciple.
hunks.sol: Then I respectfully saluted the old physician standing there with a composed expression and the young Disciple beside him.

hunks.baseline: The two men returned the salute.
hunks.sol: The two returned my salute.

hunks.baseline: “I will help my Master and do everything I can as well.”
hunks.sol: “I, too, will assist my Master and do everything in my power.”

hunks.baseline: Do everything one could and leave the rest to heaven.
hunks.sol: Do everything one could, then leave the rest to heaven.

hunks.baseline: We had done everything humans could do. Now all that remained was to leave it to the heavens.
hunks.sol: We had done everything within human power. All that remained was to entrust the outcome to the heavens.

hunks.baseline: *Whoever you are, if you help me just this once, I will never forget it.*
hunks.sol: *Whoever you are, if you help me just this once, I’ll never forget it.*

hunks.baseline: I did not believe in gods, but I did believe that an omniscient and omnipotent being existed somewhere above the heavens.
hunks.sol: I did not believe in gods, but I did believe there was some omniscient and omnipotent being above the heavens.

hunks.baseline: As I offered a brief prayer to that being, whose face and name I did not know, the Divine Physician spoke in a solemn voice.
hunks.sol: As I offered a brief prayer to that being whose face and name I did not know, the Divine Physician spoke solemnly.

hunks.baseline: “Remember this. Fifteen days—fifteen days. Until then, no one may approach.”
hunks.sol: “Remember this. Fifteen days—fifteen full days. Until then, no one may approach.”

hunks.baseline: I swallowed the words hovering on the tip of my tongue. Now, I had no choice but to trust the two of them. There was only one thing I could say.
hunks.sol: I swallowed the question hovering on the tip of my tongue. I had no choice now but to trust the two of them. There was only one thing I could say.

hunks.baseline: “I will stop anyone who tries to enter, even if I have to stake my life on it.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll stop anyone who tries to enter, even if I have to stake my life on it.”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man looked down at the man before him with numb eyes.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man looked down at his victim with impassive eyes.

hunks.baseline: The man’s limbs were twisted at grotesque angles, and his skin had been flayed away. Drenched in blood, he wheezed in a voice as tiny as an ant.
hunks.sol: The man’s limbs were bent at grotesque angles, and his skin had been flayed away. Reduced to a blood-soaked ruin, he wheezed in a voice as faint as an ant’s.

hunks.baseline: “Aren’t you leaving out the most important part?”
hunks.sol: “You’ve left out the most important part.”

hunks.baseline: Blood tears flowed from his one remaining eye, while the trouser legs already soaked in blood grew wet with urine.
hunks.sol: Bloody tears streamed from his one remaining eye. His trouser legs, already drenched in blood, darkened further with urine.

hunks.baseline: The man forced out a trembling voice.
hunks.sol: The man forced out a trembling plea.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man watched the man’s eyes, which looked ready to go out at any moment, then clicked his tongue.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man stared into the man’s fading eye, then clicked his tongue.

hunks.baseline: “Judging by this, it seems you were telling the truth.”
hunks.sol: “It seems you really are telling the truth.”

hunks.baseline: If he had begged to be spared, there might still have been room for doubt. But once the word *death* escaped his lips, the middle-aged man had to accept that he was telling the truth.
hunks.sol: If he had begged for his life, there might still have been room for doubt. But now that he was begging for death, the middle-aged man had no choice but to accept it.

hunks.baseline: Until now, no one had ever lied to the middle-aged man.
hunks.sol: No one had ever lied before him and gotten away with it.

hunks.baseline: With one exception—the Poison King, Tang Taesang.
hunks.sol: No one except the Poison King, Tang Taesang.

hunks.baseline: “I’ve seen your half-day’s worth of courage. You can rest now.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve seen the extent of your half-day’s courage. You may rest now.”

hunks.baseline: Along with the sound of a single gust of wind, the blood-soaked head jerked backward. A flick of the middle-aged man’s finger had pierced the man between the brows, and he died with a peaceful expression.
hunks.sol: A thin gust cut through the air, snapping the blood-soaked head backward. The middle-aged man’s flicked finger had pierced the victim between the brows, leaving him dead with a peaceful expression.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man stared down at the body of the man who had been a member of a collateral branch of the Sichuan Tang Clan and an operative of the Green Shadow Squad. Then he stretched out a hand.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man gazed down at the corpse of the Sichuan Tang Clan collateral relative who had served in the Green Shadow Squad, then extended a hand.

hunks.baseline: A pit a zhang deep appeared with a thunderous roar.
hunks.sol: A thunderous roar rang out as a pit one zhang deep opened in the ground.

hunks.baseline: The five bodies scattered around him were neatly stacked inside it, and the entire process—from burying them beneath the earth to covering the pit—took no more than an instant.
hunks.sol: The five corpses scattered nearby were neatly stacked inside it and covered with earth, all within moments.

hunks.baseline: “The Green Shadow Squad… So those gnats have latched on.”
hunks.sol: “The Green Shadow Squad… So those gnats have latched on to me.”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man muttered quietly as he looked beyond the winding mountain ridge. His gaze was directed west, toward the Sichuan Tang Clan.
hunks.sol: Muttering under his breath, the middle-aged man looked beyond the winding mountain ridge. West, toward the Sichuan Tang Clan.

hunks.baseline: It had been a mistake. The Poison King’s resistance had been stronger than expected, and it had taken considerable time to drive the poison out. He had even lost one of his arms.
hunks.sol: That had been a mistake. The Poison King’s resistance had been fiercer than expected, and purging the poison had taken considerable time. It had even cost him an arm.

hunks.baseline: Emei or Qingcheng might have been another matter, but the Sichuan Tang Clan was highly vigilant and thoroughly defended. Even for him, storming the place alone with one arm missing would be too much.
hunks.sol: Emei or Qingcheng might have been another matter, but the Sichuan Tang Clan was exceptionally vigilant and heavily defended. Even for him, storming the place alone after losing an arm would be too much.

hunks.baseline: All preparations were complete to hunt the three tigers crouching in Sichuan—Emei, Qingcheng, and the Tang Clan.
hunks.sol: All preparations were complete to hunt the three tigers crouching there—Emei, Qingcheng, and the Tang Clan.

hunks.baseline: It was time to call in the hunters.
hunks.sol: It was time to summon the hunters.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man moved as smoothly as if he were sliding. With every step, distance vanished beneath him and the scenery blurred past.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man moved as though gliding. Distance vanished with every step, and the scenery swept past him.

hunks.baseline: Without hesitation, the middle-aged man reached out and touched the cliff.
hunks.sol: Without hesitation, the middle-aged man reached out and placed a hand against the cliff.

hunks.baseline: The next moment—
hunks.sol: The next instant—

hunks.baseline: Along with a resonant hum, the cliff collapsed.
hunks.sol: A resonant hum rang out, and the cliff collapsed.

hunks.baseline: No. It would have been more accurate to say that space itself had warped. The weathered stones and boulders vanished, revealing a vast hollow that had been hidden from sight.
hunks.sol: No. It would be more accurate to say that space itself had warped. The weathered stones and boulders vanished, revealing a vast hollow concealed behind them.

hunks.baseline: *The sorcerers’ Mystic Gate Formation. It never stops being impressive.*
hunks.sol: *The sorcerers’ Mystic Gate Formations never cease to amaze me.*

hunks.baseline: At the center of the hollow, where darkness had settled thickly, the middle-aged man stood in the middle of a strange pattern carved into the floor and raised his internal energy.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man strode into the darkness blanketing the hollow. At its heart, he stopped in the center of a strange pattern carved into the floor and drew upon his internal energy.

hunks.baseline: The instant the dark red haze pouring from his entire body touched the pattern—
hunks.sol: A dark red haze poured from his entire body.
The instant it touched the pattern—

hunks.baseline: At the middle-aged man’s cry, the pattern began to shine. A black flash—dark yet bright, impossible to describe—filled the hollow.
hunks.sol: At the middle-aged man’s cry, the pattern blazed to life. A black flash—dark yet bright, impossible to describe—filled the entire hollow.

hunks.baseline: Then, filling the space left behind after the light vanished, came a thunderous roar.
hunks.sol: Then the light vanished, and a thunderous chorus filled the space it left behind.

hunks.baseline: Hundreds of tiger hunters in pitch-black robes stood before him, their eyes devoid of emotion and their auras as sharp as blades.
hunks.sol: Hundreds of tiger hunters stood before him in pitch-black robes, their eyes devoid of emotion and their auras sharp as blades.

hunks.baseline: A faint smile formed at the lips of the middle-aged man—the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
hunks.sol: A faint smile touched the lips of the middle-aged man—the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
